name: v1.7 NEXUS-TRIAD two-arm evidence benchmark — normal AnkiDroid (stock FSRS) vs NEXUS-TRIAD scheduling
based_on: ../v16_nexus_mix2_benchmark (sim15/sim16 imported UNMODIFIED: behavior truth, FSRS wrapper, evaluator, env, DPI endpoint); v14/v15/v16 files untouched
motivation: User directive: 'now same memory benchmarks but simulate using of normal anki droid and nexus triad ones no hallucination or guesses evidence based result' + 'build toward a TRIAD-native memory model only when you have evidence showing which aspect of human recall the current FSRS-centered approach fails to capture. Then compare the new model against FSRS using real, held-out outcomes.' v1.7 therefore (a) runs the two-arm scheduling benchmark on the v1.6 truth model, and (b) logs per-review event diagnostics that are compared against the SAME diagnostics computed on REAL learner data (Duolingo HLR public dataset, English learners) in the companion real-data pipeline.
seed_policy: IDENTICAL to the v1.6 confirmation block (20261101). The shared arm fsrs_multitype MUST reproduce the v1.6 confirmation-base numbers bit-exactly (replication audit in analyze17). No calibration block is needed because the TRIAD arm's policy knobs are FROZEN EX ANTE from the v1.6 frozen policy (p075_prot) — no re-tuning is performed (anti-circularity).

fsrs_multitype.role: Arm A — 'normal AnkiDroid': stock FSRS scheduling, scheduler's own due order, grinds to budget. Verbatim sim16.policy.FsrsMultiType16. This is the released v1.8 APK's scheduling behavior (its TRIAD layer is a passive tracker that does not modify scheduling).

nexus_triad.role: Arm B — NEXUS-TRIAD owns scheduling. FSRS remains the authoritative per-card memory engine (intervals NEVER modified: the alpha=0 gate is respected — no contextual term touches interval math). TRIAD owns: (1) review prioritization — per-skill due queues sorted by ASCENDING scheduler-predicted retrievability (most fragile first) before the v1.5 dishabituation interleave (fragile material is reviewed while the session is fresh); (2) session control — goal line at 75% of budget with due-core protection (FROZEN from the v1.6 frozen policy p075_prot; not re-tuned); (3) cold-start priors — weakest-skill-biased new-card intake quota (v1.5 mix rule, unchanged).

frozen_knobs.source: v1.6 outputs/frozen_policy.json (declared ex ante; no v1.7 tuning)

triad_no_risk_order.role: descriptive: TRIAD with the risk-ordering layer OFF (queues in scheduler-native most-overdue order) — isolates the ordering effect; pacing knobs identical

triad_no_pacing.role: descriptive: TRIAD with the goal line OFF (grinds to budget) — isolates the pacing effect; risk ordering on

scenarios_run.comment: Declared subset of the v1.6 stress grid, chosen to bound the layers NEW or LOAD-BEARING in v1.7: fatigue->quit channel (ordering front-loads fragile work early, which only matters if fatigue penalizes performance), doubled monotony (interleave interacts with ordering), and the two skeptical cells (mechanical floor). The full 9-scenario grid for the pacing knobs already exists in v1.6 and is not re-run.

v17_preregistration.P1_no_harm_primary: |ret28_diff(nexus_triad - fsrs_multitype)| <= 0.02 on the confirmation block (paired CRN, same statistic as v1.6 K3). This is the PRIMARY claim: TRIAD-owned scheduling must not harm learning.
v17_preregistration.P2_efficiency_secondary: DPI/hour relative gain of nexus_triad vs fsrs_multitype >= +5% with bootstrap CI excluding 0 (v1.6 K1 rule, carried). Point estimate and CI reported as-is either way; no superiority claim without the CI.
v17_preregistration.P3_ordering_effect_exploratory: nexus_triad vs triad_no_risk_order: DPI/h and ret28 paired diffs (exploratory attribution of the NEW layer; no pass/fail).
v17_preregistration.P4_honesty: v1.6 K4/K5 definitions: due_completion_rate diff >= -0.02; premature-quit rate and quit-intensity diffs reported with CIs.
v17_preregistration.P5_diagnostics_descriptive: per-review event rows (scheduler-predicted retrievability before each review, outcome, session context) are logged for BOTH arms and analyzed ONLY descriptively: FSRS calibration residuals stratified by session position/elapsed time/workload/absence. In-simulation residuals are properties of the DECLARED truth model; the same stratification is computed on real learner data by the companion real-data pipeline (scripts/v17/real_*.py) — the real data is the evidence base for the TRIAD-native memory-model question, the simulation only bounds scheduling-level consequences.
v17_preregistration.P6_stress: session-minutes diff, quit diff and ret diff per scenario with CIs; mechanical floor = hard_skeptical session diff.
v17_preregistration.analysis: paired CRN diffs per (rep, learner_id); 95% cluster bootstrap (cluster = learner_id, n=2000); the confirmation block is the ONLY evidence; the shared arm must replicate v1.6 bit-exactly (any drift is a bug, not noise)

event_log_fields.comment: Logged by a transparent scheduler proxy; consumes NO RNG and cannot alter behavior (delegation only), verified by the replication audit.
event_log_fields.fields: arm, rep, learner_id, day, t_min, elapsed_min, event_idx_in_session, skill, item_id, grade, correct, r_before (scheduler-predicted retrievability immediately BEFORE the grade was applied), s_before (scheduler stability estimate before update), due_count_session_start

honesty.simulation_not_humans: every v1.7 scheduling number is a property of the declared simulation; no real learner has been measured by the simulation
honesty.released_apk_status: the released v1.8 APK's TRIAD is a passive tracker (its onAnswer record is discarded after FSRS has already scheduled); Arm A reproduces that scheduling behavior; Arm B evaluates the TRIAD scheduling DESIGN, not the shipped APK
honesty.alpha_gate: interval decisions remain pure FSRS in BOTH arms (alpha=0): the simulation contains no interval-modification effect to find, by design, until real held-out evidence justifies alpha>0
honesty.no_circular_tuning: TRIAD knobs are frozen from the v1.6 frozen policy; the v1.7 truth constants are the v1.5/v1.6 constants untouched; no knob was tuned on v1.7 runs
